guidelineVersions: European Malignant Hyperthermia Group 2024 guideline (Br J Anaesth 2025), noted for comparison

related.why: Another anaesthetic emergency the surgical team helps to manage

brief.scenario: Mr Liam Hebditch, 23, weighs 80 kg and is having a laparoscopic appendicectomy. Anaesthesia was induced with suxamethonium and maintained with sevoflurane. Twenty minutes in, the anaesthetist says his end-tidal CO2 keeps rising despite increased ventilation and his heart rate is 130.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on recognition and management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Recognise, declare, stop the trigger, dantrolene, cool, treat the consequences, refer.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Waiting for the temperature to rise before calling it malignant hyperthermia.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This could be malignant hyperthermia. Let's declare it and call for help and the MH kit."

grid.label: Recognition
grid.fail: Attributes the signs to light anaesthesia or sepsis and carries on.
grid.pass: Suspects MH: unexplained rising end-tidal CO2 and tachycardia after a volatile agent or suxamethonium, with rigidity and later rising temperature.
grid.high: Knows temperature often hasn't risen when the diagnosis is made; notes masseter spasm, hyperkalaemia, acidosis and arrhythmias.

grid.label: Declare and call for help
grid.fail: Doesn't declare the emergency, or keeps operating as normal.
grid.pass: Declares suspected MH, calls for help and the MH kit, and finishes or stops the operation as quickly as safely possible.
grid.high: Takes a role: helps reconstitute dantrolene, sends a runner for ice and cold fluids, and follows the crisis card.

grid.label: Remove the trigger
grid.fail: Only turns the volatile agent down.
grid.pass: Turn off and remove the vaporiser; 100% oxygen at maximum flow; minute ventilation 2–3 times normal; activated charcoal filters.
grid.high: Filters go on both the inspiratory and expiratory limbs; no further volatile agents or suxamethonium.

grid.label: Dantrolene
grid.fail: Doesn't know dantrolene, or gives one small dose.
grid.pass: Dantrolene 2–3 mg/kg IV (actual body weight), then 1 mg/kg every 5 minutes until end-tidal CO2 is below 6 kPa and core temperature below 38.5°C.
grid.high: Each 20 mg vial needs 60 ml of sterile water, so several people mix it; reappraise the diagnosis after 10 mg/kg.

grid.label: Cooling and consequences
grid.fail: Doesn't cool, or gives calcium routinely for hyperkalaemia rather than only in extremis (UK 2020 guideline).
grid.pass: Active cooling; core temperature and arterial line; catheter; hyperkalaemia with insulin-glucose or bicarbonate; bicarbonate for acidosis.
grid.high: Calcium only in extremis (UK 2020 guideline); aims for urine over 2 ml/kg/h for myoglobinuria; watches for DIC and compartment syndrome.

grid.label: After the crisis
grid.fail: Sends him back to the ward once he looks stable.
grid.pass: HDU or ICU for at least 24 hours if dantrolene was needed; watch for recrudescence.
grid.high: Recrudescence has been reported up to 14 hours later: further dantrolene if it recurs, not routinely as prophylaxis.

grid.label: Referral and family
grid.fail: Doesn't tell the patient, GP or family.
grid.pass: Consultant anaesthetist refers him to the UK MH Unit in Leeds; patient and GP informed before discharge.
grid.high: Genetic basis (RYR1, CACNA1S, STAC3); blood relatives treated as at risk until tested; future anaesthetics avoid volatiles and suxamethonium.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He's probably light. The anaesthetist should turn the gas up.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: His temperature is 38.2 and he's rigid.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll carry on and finish the appendix; it may be sepsis.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: It's malignant hyperthermia. What's the first step?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: He's stable now. Where does he go?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Back to the ward with regular observations.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Rising end-tidal CO2 and tachycardia after suxamethonium and sevoflurane: I'd suspect malignant hyperthermia, especially if he's rigid.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What do you do as the surgeon?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Declare it, call for help and the MH kit, and finish or stop the operation as quickly as safely possible.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Turn off and remove the vaporiser, 100% oxygen at maximum flow, increase ventilation two to three times, and put in charcoal filters.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Dantrolene 2 to 3 mg/kg IV on actual weight, so 160 to 240 mg, then 1 mg/kg every 5 minutes until end-tidal CO2 is below 6 kPa and temperature below 38.5.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Active cooling, core temperature and an arterial line, a catheter. Treat hyperkalaemia with insulin and glucose or bicarbonate, and acidosis with bicarbonate.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: He's stable. Where does he go?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: HDU or ICU for at least 24 hours, because it can recur.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The consultant anaesthetist refers him to the MH Unit in Leeds, and he and his GP are told before discharge.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: His temperature may still be normal; that doesn't exclude it. I'd also ask about jaw stiffness after the suxamethonium, and check potassium and a blood gas.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll pack and close quickly, then help mix dantrolene. Can someone bring ice and cold fluids, and read the crisis card?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Charcoal filters on both the inspiratory and expiratory limbs. No more volatile or suxamethonium.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How much dantrolene is that practically?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Each 20 mg vial needs 60 ml of sterile water, so we need several people mixing. If we reach 10 mg/kg, we should rethink the diagnosis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Only in extremis in MH; insulin-glucose and bicarbonate first. I'd aim for urine over 2 ml/kg/h because of myoglobinuria, and watch for DIC and compartment syndrome.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you give more dantrolene prophylactically?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No, but recrudescence has been reported up to 14 hours later, so he needs close monitoring and more dantrolene if it recurs.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's genetic, usually RYR1, sometimes CACNA1S or STAC3. His blood relatives should be treated as at risk until tested, and he must avoid volatiles and suxamethonium in future.

failures.move: Waiting for a high temperature before suspecting MH.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: delay to treatment increases mortality and complications.

failures.move: Not knowing dantrolene or under-dosing it.
failures.consequence: The hypermetabolic reaction continues: hyperkalaemia, arrhythmia and death.

failures.move: Discharging without informing the patient, GP or family.
failures.consequence: Relatives may be exposed to triggering agents in future.
Diverts the team from the crisis.

recovery.line: Three things together: remove the trigger, give dantrolene, cool him.

recovery.when: Asked what you do as the surgeon
recovery.line: Finish quickly and safely, then help mix dantrolene and cool him.

knowledge.fact: Triggers: potent inhalational agents and suxamethonium.
Dantrolene 2–3 mg/kg, then 1 mg/kg every 5 min until ETCO2 below 6 kPa and core temperature below 38.5°C.
Each 20 mg vial of dantrolene is mixed with 60 ml of sterile water; the 250 mg preparation (Ryanodex) is not licensed in the UK.
Calcium only in extremis; HDU or ICU for at least 24 h if dantrolene was needed.
Refer to the UK MH Unit in Leeds; warn blood relatives.
EMHG 2024 gives dantrolene 2–2.5 mg/kg repeated every 10 min; this UK station follows the Association of Anaesthetists 2020.

recall.say: "I suspect malignant hyperthermia: call for help and the MH kit."

numbers.meaning: minimum HDU/ICU stay if dantrolene needed

recall.trap: A normal temperature doesn't exclude MH.
recall.finish: HDU/ICU, referral to Leeds MH Unit, family warned.

sources.name: Hopkins PM, Girard T, Dalay S, et al. Malignant hyperthermia 2020: guideline from the Association of Anaesthetists. Anaesthesia 2021;76:655–64
sources.supports: Triggers (potent inhalational agents, suxamethonium); rising ETCO2 and tachycardia; temperature often not raised at diagnosis; masseter spasm; remove vaporiser, 100% oxygen at maximum flow, minute ventilation 2–3 times normal, charcoal filters on inspiratory and expiratory limbs; dantrolene 2–3 mg/kg on actual body weight then 1 mg/kg every 5 min to ETCO2 <6 kPa and core temperature <38.5°C; reappraise at 10 mg/kg; 20 mg vials in 60 ml sterile water; Ryanodex 250 mg not licensed in UK; active cooling; hyperkalaemia with bicarbonate and/or insulin-glucose, calcium only in extremis; urine output >2 ml/kg/h; DIC; compartment syndrome; recrudescence up to 14 h, no prophylactic dantrolene; HDU/ICU at least 24 h if dantrolene given; referral to Leeds MH Unit; inform patient, GP and blood relatives; RYR1, CACNA1S, STAC3

sources.name: Glahn KPE, et al. Recognition and management of a malignant hyperthermia crisis: updated 2024 guideline from the European Malignant Hyperthermia Group. Br J Anaesth 2025;134:221–3
sources.supports: European guideline: dantrolene 2–2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated every 10 minutes until the hypermetabolic signs resolve; the UK station follows the Association of Anaesthetists 2020 guideline

media.description: Anaesthetic monitor trend showing a progressive rise in end-tidal CO2 and heart rate over 20 minutes despite increased minute ventilation

partner.opening: The anaesthetist tells you end-tidal CO2 keeps rising and heart rate is 130. What's happening?

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about temperature and muscle tone
reveals.finding: Temperature 37.6°C now 38.2°C. Jaw stiff after suxamethonium; limbs now rigid.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for a blood gas
reveals.finding: pH 7.12, PaCO2 9.8 kPa, lactate 6, K+ 6.9 mmol/L.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about response to treatment
reveals.finding: After 240 mg dantrolene: ETCO2 5.6 kPa, temperature 38.1°C, HR 95.

push.question: How is the trigger removed?
push.expect: Vaporiser off and removed, 100% O2 max flow, 2–3x ventilation, charcoal filters.

push.question: What dose of dantrolene?
push.expect: 2–3 mg/kg, then 1 mg/kg every 5 min to goals.

push.question: How do you treat the potassium?
push.expect: Insulin-glucose or bicarbonate; calcium only in extremis.

curveballs.prompt: Someone suggests the 250 mg dantrolene vial because it mixes faster.
curveballs.safeAnswer: That preparation isn't licensed in the UK; use the standard 20 mg vials with 60 ml sterile water each.

curveballs.prompt: His temperature is only 37.6°C. Could it still be MH?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Yes. Temperature often hasn't risen at diagnosis; treat on rising CO2 and tachycardia.

curveballs.prompt: Four hours later his end-tidal CO2 rises again on ICU.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Recrudescence: give further dantrolene, 1 mg/kg in the first instance.
